text: Candidate synthesis: turn P\x27s Energy Society discussion phase into an empirical stress test of Q\x27s peer-discipline proposition. Q 1649-1699 says correlated private types plus separation and sufficiently large quadratic peer-score rewards implement any feasible rule; P 209-225 has costly, public, non-binding recommendations and P 794-802 observes selfish collision/donation recommendations. The key advance may be a resource-bounded version: when communication and rewards consume the same survival budget, what is the minimum score scale needed for truthful/obedient allocation, and does it improve collision-adjusted group energy net of inference cost?

I will develop one concrete bridge: use Energy Society as a finite-budget stress test of Q peer-discipline. Q Prop. support-wise implementability relies on a sufficiently large peer-score multiplier and effectively free/unbounded rewards; P makes every token and transfer survival-relevant. I will derive the finite-reward threshold, map observable P logs to its terms, and propose a discriminating experiment rather than claim P already tests the theorem.

Cross-check on the shared peer-discipline bridge: P does not yet test Q Prop. 1697. P elicits recommendations, not private type reports; its MMLU answers provide ex post ground truth (P 173-176); and Q proves truthful/obedient play is an equilibrium but does not establish equilibrium selection or resistance to coordinated/common misreports. Any paper must present P as a new testbed modification, include an oracle-score control, and measure collusive or pooling equilibria rather than call current findings a falsification.

Finite-budget derivation: Q's proof gives truthful-report score loss Lambda*delta and maximum residual utility gain M, hence its own construction needs Lambda >= M/delta (Q 1704-1734). It separately forces obedience with -infinity off-path rewards (Q 1687-1702). In Energy Society neither lever is free: energy is survival capital (P 147-159), transfers cannot exceed current balance (P 166-167), and communication itself costs energy (P 209). Thus the publishable question is a boundary result, not merely an experiment: characterize implementability under bounded penalties/rewards and costly reports, where small belief separation delta makes the required score scale explode and finite survival wealth can make Q's construction infeasible.

Sharpened synthesis in emmy/synthesis.md: test Q peer discipline under P-style bounded, budget-balanced survival rewards. Q proof gives construction-specific threshold Lambda*delta >= M (Q 1704-1734). In P, feasible Lambda is capped by current energy/limited liability, predicting discipline fails near deactivation. Experiment should elicit probabilistic peer-action forecasts, randomize score stakes, and compare minted diagnostic scores with escrowed budget-balanced scores; primary welfare must be endowment-adjusted total energy net of communication cost.

Critical qualification to our shared idea: existing P logs do not test Q. P recommendations are public action proposals, not private type reports or beta_i belief distributions; model identity is not a private type. Also minted score energy mechanically raises P cooperative welfare. A clean study must create randomized correlated private signals within model identity, elicit probabilistic forecasts, and use budget-balanced escrow. Lambda*delta >= M is sufficient for Q particular score construction, not yet a general bounded-mechanism impossibility theorem.

Incorporating ada cross-check: even above Lambda >= M/delta, Q establishes an equilibrium, not selection or robustness to coordinated/pooling reports. Add an oracle-score control and explicitly measure pooling/collusive equilibria. Also separate truth-telling incentives from obedience because Q obtains the latter with off-path -infinity rewards, unavailable under limited liability.

Refinement of the theorem target: communication cost by itself does not necessarily harm truthfulness if every structured report has equal token cost; it matters through report-dependent cost and through net welfare. The hard constraint is bounded reward variation. For any prescribed action, let D be the largest private plus continuation-value gain from disobedience. If an agent's feasible reward spread at current energy is B<D, no reward schedule can induce obedience. For reports, Q's specific construction needs Lambda*delta >= M, with M expanded to include report-cost and dynamic continuation differences. Near deactivation, feasible negative penalties are wealth-limited even if nominal scores are large.

Discriminating Energy Society experiment: introduce planted correlated private signals about each round's latent job state, so truthful types are observed by the experimenter; estimate beta_i and delta on held-out runs. Compare (i) P's unscored discussion, (ii) Q peer scoring across a Lambda sweep paid from survival energy, (iii) the same scores paid externally (free-reward benchmark), (iv) oracle proper scoring against eventual job outcomes, and (v) centralized/report-free allocation. Outcomes: truthful reports, obedience, collisions, total job energy net of all inference/score costs, and deactivation. Vary starting wealth and signal separation. Q predicts a threshold near Lambda=M/delta in the free arm; the pair-specific hypothesis is that the threshold becomes infeasible or welfare-negative under low wealth/small delta, with pooling/collusion explicitly audited.

I am converging on one line: 'resource-bounded peer discipline.' It directly relaxes Q's explicitly free/unbounded-reward benchmark (Q 267) using P's endogenous survival budget and dynamic testbed, while P supplies the observed need (costly discussion coordinates but carries selfish messages, P 623-628 and 794-802). I will check Emmy's derivation/objections once more, then declare ready with unresolved identification and equilibrium-selection issues explicit.

Best account of pair: changed broad question to: when peer scores must be funded from agents' survival capital, can correlated reports still discipline both reports and actions, and at what welfare cost? Theory: extend Q's static benchmark to finite-horizon limited liability, separating report threshold Lambda*delta >= M (construction-specific) from obedience feasibility B>=D; characterize the wealth/signal-separation region and net-welfare optimum rather than assume arbitrarily large Lambda. Evidence/motivation: Q explicitly assumes free, unbounded rewards (Q 267) and uses -infinity for disobedience (Q 1687-1702); P makes tokens costly and energy necessary for activity (P 147-170), finds discussion reduces collisions but consumes energy (P 209, 619-628), and observes selfish recommendations (P 773-802). Empirical contribution: planted correlated private signals, stakes x wealth x delta design, survival-funded versus externally minted scores, oracle and centralized controls. Unresolved: elicited signals may not represent natural LLM preferences/capabilities; delta and dynamic M,D require estimation; budget balance and limited liability need precise mechanism definitions; Q gives partial implementation, so pooling/collusion and equilibrium selection may defeat predictions.

Cross-check of #9/#12 and correction to emmy/synthesis.md: budget balance alone does not cap score scale by the reporter current energy. Limited liability caps losses, while peers or pooled escrow can fund positive prizes. Define B as the maximum outcome-contingent reward spread under the exact funding rule. Self-escrow makes B wealth-dependent near deactivation; pooled escrow makes B depend on group wealth/contribution rules. The general obedience statement B<D is valid once B and the deviation gain D are conditioned on the same history, signal, and prescribed action; it is a necessary one-shot incentive inequality, not yet a full dynamic impossibility theorem.

Incorporating Emmy #14: replace the loose claim that survival wealth caps any budget-balanced score with a funding-rule-specific constraint. At a fixed history h, signal/type, and prescribed action, define B(h) as the maximum difference in feasible continuation-inclusive transfers across outcomes under the exact mechanism. If the best deviation gains D(h)>B(h), obedience is impossible at that history. Self-escrow makes B(h) depend on the agent current energy; pooled escrow makes it depend on group escrow and contribution/withdrawal rules; externally minted scores need not have either cap. Likewise, Lambda*delta>=M only certifies Q particular quadratic construction, with feasible Lambda determined by score normalization and funding. This distinction strengthens the proposed self-versus-pooled-versus-minted experiment.
